items.question: What attainments make a practitioner dear to the yoginīs?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation are attained together.
Great accomplishment arises for the practitioner.
Such attainment brings favor from the yoginīs.
items.inference: A practitioner who attains enjoyment, liberation, and great accomplishment becomes dear to the yoginīs.
items.plain_english: He may attain enjoyment, liberation, and great accomplishment, and become dear to the yoginīs.

rows.grounds: describes the chapter as issued forth

items.question: Which chapter concludes after the teaching emerged in Candra-dvīpa?
premises: The teaching has emerged in Candra-dvīpa.
A chapter is being numbered in sequence.
The sequence reaches the ninth chapter.
items.inference: The ninth chapter concludes following the emergence in Candra-dvīpa.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the ninth chapter, which emerged in Candra-dvīpa.

items.question: How is the self visualized when surrounded by fire in this practice?
premises: The self is encircled by fire.
The posture involves only one foot.
The self is established in that stance.
items.inference: The practice visualizes the self surrounded by fire and standing on one foot.
items.plain_english: One should visualize the self surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

rows.grounds: thing requested to be made clear

items.question: What clarification about knowledge is requested from the deity now?
premises: A determination of knowledge is sought.
The request is addressed to the deity.
The seeker asks for it to be made manifest now.
items.inference: The deity is asked to reveal the determination of knowledge at this moment.
items.plain_english: O God, make manifest to me today the determination of knowledge.

rows.grounds: second member indicating sets of eight

items.question: What division into groups of eight is sought to be known completely?
premises: A division consists of eight groups of eight.
Complete knowledge of this division is desired.
The understanding is sought in an exhaustive manner.
items.inference: The seeker wishes to know fully and exhaustively the division into eight groups of eight.
uncertainties: anantathā may mean 'in infinite detail' or 'without end'
items.plain_english: And I wish to know fully and endlessly the division into eight groups of eight.

rows.grounds: first member of compound qualifying place
states the result in that place

items.question: How does the wheel become quickly accomplished in the secret place?
premises: There is a secret place associated with the wheel.
The wheel can be accomplished there.
The accomplishment occurs quickly.
items.inference: In the secret place, O Bhairava, the wheel is accomplished quickly.
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, tell how the wheel is quickly accomplished in the secret place.

rows.grounds: first member of compound describing rarity

items.question: Why is the question asked by the great goddess considered difficult even for gods?
premises: The goddess has asked a question.
The speaker approves the question strongly.
The matter asked about is hard for gods to obtain.
items.inference: The goddess has asked about a matter that is well-posed yet difficult even for the gods to obtain.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O great goddess. You have asked me about something hard for even the gods to obtain.

rows.grounds: identifies the location or nature as brahmarandhra
seed syllable located in the forehead

items.question: Which seed syllables are assigned to the brahmarandhra and the forehead?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with the brahmarandhra.
The syllable laṃ is associated with the forehead.
These assignments locate syllables in the body.
items.inference: The syllable kṣa belongs to the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ belongs to the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form though often used for the forehead region
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is in the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Which seed syllables are placed in the throat region and the heart?
premises: The syllable ṣa is placed in the throat region.
The syllable śa is placed in the heart.
These placements continue the bodily mapping of syllables.
items.inference: The syllable ṣa belongs to the throat region and the syllable śa belongs to the heart.
items.plain_english: Then the syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is in the heart.

items.question: What instruction follows after the place-wheels have been declared?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared.
Each wheel has an associated meditation.
The listener is invited to hear that meditation.
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the teaching turns to their meditation.
items.plain_english: Thus the place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: How is the divine lotus of the first octad described for meditation?
premises: The lotus has eight spokes or petals.
The lotus is divine in nature.

items.inference: The meditation envisions a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.
uncertainties: āraṃ may be read as spokes or petals depending on context
items.plain_english: Visualize a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.

items.question: What conduct should a practitioner adopt after gaining mental equipoise through practice?
premises: Practice leads to an even mind.
Village duties bind one to ordinary life.
The teaching prescribes abandonment of such duties.
items.inference: Through practice one becomes even-minded and should abandon village duties.
uncertainties: grāma-dharmañ may refer broadly to conventional social obligations
items.plain_english: Through practice, becoming even-minded, one should abandon the duties of village life.

rows.grounds: first member of compound describing hearing

first member of compound naming paralysis

items.question: What supernatural powers arise from this stage of practice?
premises: Knowledge of distant hearing arises.
The power to paralyze bonds arises likewise.
These are presented as attained results.
items.inference: This practice yields distant hearing and the power of immobilization.
uncertainties: pāśa-stobham may mean paralysis of bonds or paralysis caused by bonds
items.plain_english: O beloved, one gains knowledge of distant hearing and likewise the power to paralyze.

items.question: What further results are briefly attributed to this practice?
premises: Immortality is attained.
Transformation is attained likewise.
The teaching states these results in brief.
items.inference: In brief, the practice brings immortality and transformation.
uncertainties: parivartanam could mean transformation, reversal, or transference
items.plain_english: Likewise, O goddess, in brief one attains immortality and transformation.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled lotus characterized in meditation?
premises: The second lotus has eight petals.
It is associated with meditation on fiery radiance.
It is described as well illuminated.
items.inference: The second eight-petaled lotus is brightly illuminated through meditation on fire.
items.plain_english: The second is an eight-petaled lotus, well illuminated by meditation on fire.

items.question: What ability arises for one whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation?
premises: The mind becomes absorbed in one-pointed meditation.
Such absorption grants creative power.
The practitioner can produce many forms.
items.inference: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.
items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can create many forms.

rows.grounds: expresses power to withdraw or destroy

items.question: What destructive power is attributed to the practitioner when angered?
premises: The practitioner may become angry.
Anger activates a destructive power.

items.inference: When angered, the practitioner can destroy the entire triple world, both moving and unmoving.
items.plain_english: When angry, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.plain_english: The third is the great wheel, which liberates one from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual benefits result from this wheel's practice?
premises: Wrinkles and grey hair are destroyed.
Seeing from very far away is gained.
These benefits arise together.
items.inference: The practice removes signs of aging and grants distant vision.
items.plain_english: It brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the ability to see from very far away.

items.question: How should a devoted practitioner cultivate multiple forms in meditation?
premises: The practice is to be done in solitude.
Meditation can produce many forms.
The practitioner must be intent on that practice.
items.inference: In solitude, being intent on meditation, one should create many forms.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, create many forms.

items.question: What result comes to one devoted to constant practice?
premises: Constant practice is maintained.
The practitioner is intent on that practice.
Such devotion produces immortality.
items.inference: One devoted to constant practice indeed attains immortality.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one who is intent on constant practice attains immortality.

rows.grounds: first member of compound with death

items.question: How does abstention from eating affect death associated with aging?
premises: Non-eating is practiced day by day.
Aging and death are linked conditions.
The practice leads beyond that death.
items.inference: Through daily non-eating, one will go beyond death associated with aging.
uncertainties: nāśanena may mean fasting or complete abstention; gamiṣyate may imply overcoming rather than undergoing
items.plain_english: By daily abstention from food, one will go beyond death caused by aging.

items.question: What bodily form results from constant yogic practice over time?
premises: Yogic practice is performed constantly.
The practice continues over a long period.
The body takes on a youthful form of sixteen years.
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one may attain the form of a sixteen-year-old.
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one may attain the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What power arises from continually contemplating a smoke-colored form?
premises: A smoke-colored form is contemplated continually.
Contemplation generates yogic power.
That power can affect the triple world.
items.inference: By always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one may shake the triple world.

items.plain_english: O beloved, by always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world.
